claims.text: Enhanced cooling during sputter deposition refines the grain size of non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films.
Enhanced deposition cooling increases local chemical heterogeneity in these films.
Enhanced deposition cooling increases local strain heterogeneity in these films.
The resulting chemical and strain heterogeneities lower and broaden the nucleation-energy barrier of the first-order magnetostructural transition.
Lowered and broadened nucleation barriers make the magnetocaloric response less abrupt.
Lowered and broadened nucleation barriers reduce hysteresis under low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The standard as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi baseline has a relatively coarse grain structure.
The standard as-deposited baseline has limited short-range disorder.
Varying substrate temperature from cryogenic to room temperature and applying immediate post-deposition quenching provides controlled variation of deposition cooling rate.
Otherwise identical films will be compared under applied magnetic fields below approximately 0.5–1 T.
Grain refinement and associated local chemical and stress distributions mediate heterogeneous nucleation of the magnetostructural transition.
Faster cooling produces a finer and more disordered grain structure.
The finer, more disordered structure decreases variability in nucleation barriers across the material.
Distributed nucleation causes the first-order magnetostructural transition to span a broader temperature interval.
Broadening the transition temperature interval reduces hysteresis.
Broadening the transition temperature interval moderates the peak magnetic entropy change.
Enhanced-cooled films will show a broader magnetocaloric transition and significantly less hysteresis than the standard as-deposited baseline.
The predicted trends will persist across the tested low-field range and will be most evident near the transition temperature.
The standard-cooling baseline exhibits a sharp, hysteretic entropy change associated with its relatively coarse microstructure.
Film thickness, extreme compositional inhomogeneity, residual stress, compositional gradients, and deposition parameters outside the tuned range may alter the predicted effects.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes transition broadening to increased heterogeneity and a broadened distribution of nucleation barriers, whereas the mechanism says the finer, more disordered structure decreases variability in those barriers. These descriptions of the barrier distribution point in opposite directions.
